nodes.description: Atlastin-1, encoded by ATL1 (SPG3A), is a dynamin-like, integral-membrane GTPase that mediates homotypic fusion of endoplasmic reticulum tubules and is required for proper formation of the interconnected tubular ER network. Most characterised ATL1 pathogenic variants impair ER-tubule fusion and network formation; because spastin, atlastin, REEP1, and reticulon-2 interact in shaping the tubular ER, ER-shaping defects are proposed as a shared neuropathogenic mechanism converging on corticospinal-tract axon degeneration.

atlastins localize to the tubular ER and are required for proper network 
formation in vivo and in vitro.

nodes.description: Three dominant HSP genes converge on the endosome. NIPA1 (SPG6) is a magnesium transporter that associates with early endosomes and the cell surface and redistributes between the two with magnesium availability. WASHC5/strumpellin (SPG8) is a core subunit of the WASH complex, which activates actin nucleation at endosomes; pathogenic SPG8 alleles produce endosomal fission defects and reduce CAV1 abundance. UBAP1 (SPG80) binds ubiquitin on endosomes, and the C-terminal deletion mutant is not recruited to endosome membranes, so loss of UBAP1 function may perturb endosomal fusion and sorting of ubiquitinated cargoes.

nodes.description: DDHD1 belongs to the intracellular phospholipase A1 gene family. The study that identified DDHD1 mutations in autosomal recessive HSP showed in human cells that the pathophysiology includes altered mitochondrial architecture and bioenergetics with increased oxidative stress, and concluded that lipid metabolism is a critical HSP pathway with a deleterious impact on mitochondrial bioenergetic function. That study reported the same finding for CYP2U1; CYP2U1 is not bound on this node because SPG56 is curated as a complicated form on the complex hereditary spastic paraplegia entry.

nodes.description: The unifying pathology of HSP is degeneration of the lateral corticospinal tract axons, maximal at their distal ends in the thoracic spinal cord, with accompanying degeneration of the fasciculus gracilis (dorsal column) sensory fibers maximal in the cervico-medullary region. This pattern reflects a selective vulnerability of the longest motor and sensory axons of the central nervous system, a length-dependent distal axonopathy of the upper motor neuron. The diverse molecular causes of HSP converge on this relatively uniform corticospinal-tract degeneration, producing the shared clinical syndrome of progressive lower-limb spasticity and weakness.

nodes.description: Paraplegin, encoded by SPG7, is a nuclear-encoded mitochondrial metalloprotease (m-AAA protease) embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane, where it maintains mitochondrial protein quality by degrading damaged or unassembled respiratory-chain subunits. Loss of paraplegin function impairs oxidative phosphorylation; SPG7 patient cells show fragmented mitochondria, reduced mitochondrial mass and membrane potential, impaired oxidative phosphorylation with reduced ATP, and increased mitochondrial oxidative stress, providing a bioenergetic mechanism for corticospinal-tract neurodegeneration.

nodes.description: The convergent corticospinal-tract axonopathy produces the cardinal clinical syndrome: insidiously progressive bilateral lower-limb spasticity and weakness with hyperreflexia, crossed adductor signs, and extensor plantar (Babinski) responses. Spasticity is greatest in hamstring, quadriceps, adductor, and gastrocnemius-soleus muscles; weakness is most prominent in iliopsoas, hamstring, and tibialis anterior. This is the shared functional consequence of all genetic forms of HSP.

nodes.description: Spastin, encoded by SPAST (SPG4), is a microtubule-severing AAA ATPase that assembles into a hexameric ring and remodels neuronal microtubule arrays by pulling the C-terminal tail of tubulin through its central pore to generate a mechanical force that destabilizes the microtubule lattice. Pathogenic SPAST variants impair this severing activity, disrupting the dynamic microtubule cytoskeleton required for axonal transport and organelle distribution in long corticospinal-tract axons. Spastin loss-of-function also disrupts cytoarchitectural integrity and organellar stability (mitochondrial and ER) in corticospinal motor neurons, contributing to selective UMN vulnerability.

nodes.description: A group of HSP genes encode proteins that work together to shape the endoplasmic reticulum into sheets and tubules: REEP1 (SPG31), atlastin-1 (SPG3A) and spastin (SPG4), joined by reticulon 2 (SPG12) and REEP2 (SPG72), which also belongs to that ER-shaping family and whose original report found altered ER in fibroblasts from an affected subject. Reticulon 2 interacts with spastin through a hydrophobic region of spastin involved in ER localisation, placing these proteins in one interaction network, and the reticulon-2 work supports abnormal ER morphogenesis as a pathogenic mechanism in HSP. In SPG31 the molecular genetic mechanism is haploinsufficiency of REEP1.
